To match the latest version. Instead of potentially sending a full
`m.room.member` event in the stripped state, now all stripped state can
have the `origin_server_ts` and `unsigned` fields.

api: Move make_endpoint_url function to VersionHistory

Since it contains the only data needed, it allows to construct alternate
`VersionHistory`s without having to re-declare the whole metadata.
The function on `Metadata` now calls the method on `VersionHistory`.

client-api: Stabilize support for extended profiles

ones that support custom fields.

According to MSC4175 / Matrix 1.16

Allowing to apply `allow(clippy::exhaustive_structs)` to the whole
module instead of to the individual structs.

state-res: Use macro to initialize tracing for tests

Reduces code duplication, avoids forgetting to initialize the
subscriber, and is simpler to use.

serde: Merge PartialOrdAsRefStr derive macro into OrdAsRefStr

That way both traits are implemented at once and this makes sure that
both implementations use the same logic.

serde: Rename PartialEqAsRefStr derive macro to EqAsRefStr

And make it implement both `PartialEq` and `Eq`.

serde: Make StringEnum derive macro implement Ord, PartialOrd, Eq and PartialEq

Using the `AsRef<str>` implementation. This avoids issues like the
`Ord` implementation changing when a string that deserialized as the
fallback variant now deserializes as a supported variant.

push: Remove legacy mentions

According to MSC4210.

macros: Remove support for matrix-sdk-appservice

This crate was dropped 2 years ago.

client-api: Fix setting access token in set_profile_field::v3::Request

This is particularly important because the access token is required by
default.

api: Test VersionHistory rather than Metadata

Since the method is implemented on VersionHistory.

api: Change Metadata struct to a trait

Its fields are now associated constants with the same name converted to
uppercase.

The `metadata!` macro generates the trait implementation for a type
named `Request` by default. The type can be changed with an `@for`
setting.

`Metadata` is a supertrait of `OutgoingRequest` and `IncomingRequest`.

The goal of this is to be able in the future to change some of the
associated constants to associated types to use them in bounds.
events: add `AnySyncTimelineEvent::is_redacted` which forwards to the underlying variant

api: Make Metadata's authentication scheme an associated type

AuthScheme is changed to a trait, and its variants are now structs. The
None variant was changed to NoAuthentication.

This allows to add a bound on requests per authentication scheme.

api: Use Cow<'_, SupportedVersions> instead of &'_ SupportedVersions

This will simplify using it as an associated type.

api: Make the path builder an associated type and constant

This will allow with to use new types to stop requesting the
`SupportedVersions` on endpoints that cannot have them or don't use
them.

api: Add type to declare endpoints without version history

And allow to construct this type with the `metadata!` macro.
appservice-api: Use SinglePath as PathBuilder of requests
client-api: Use SinglePath as PathBuilder for some requests
federation-api: Use SinglePath as PathBuilder of requests
identity-service-api: Use SinglePath as PathBuilder for get_supported_versions
push-gateway-api: Use SinglePath as PathBuilder for send_event_notification

api: Default Content-Type to application/octet-stream with raw_body

Since it is usually not used with JSON bodies, and it is wrong on the
media endpoints when the Content-Type header is not overriden.

client-api: Use StandardErrorBody for ErrorBody::Standard

Avoids unnecessary duplication.

client-api: Make StandardErrorBody non-exhaustive

Since it's defined in the spec there is always a chance that a new field
might be added. This way we can prevent if from being a breaking change.

api: Move SendAccessToken to auth_scheme module

Since it is only used by authentication schemes.

api: Make Metadata::Authentication's input an associated type

ServerSignatures needs a different input, although this doesn't add
support for it (yet).

api: Require authentication type to be in scope

Instead of only supporting the types in ruma_common::api::auth_scheme.

This allows to use custom types. This is also necessary to complete the
implementation of `OutgoingRequest::add_authentication` of
`ServerSignatures`, we need to use the `XMatrix` type in
ruma-federation-api. One solution is to move `ServerSignatures` to that
crate.

common: Put http_headers module behind the api feature

It should only be used by API crates, and we will add a dependency on
the http crate in it.

common: Add constants for common Content-Type header values

To avoid possible typos.

api: Change AuthScheme::authorization_header to add_authentication

It seems like a saner API to me, and possibly more future-proof since
it allows to set more than one header.

client-api: Use AuthScheme::add_authentication in custom OutgoingRequest impls

To reduce code duplication and avoid possible errors.

api: Add method on IncomingRequest to check HTTP method

And use it everywhere.

It reduces code duplication and avoids possible mistakes.

ServerSignatures will need to access the content of the body.

push: Force PushConditionRoomCtx to be !RefUnwindSafe

Forcing `HasThreadSubscriptionFn` to be `RefUnwindSafe` is actually
problematic in the matrix-rust-sdk because for example
`tokio::sync::Mutex` is `!RefUnwindSafe`.

Since we cannot implement negative traits yet, this uses a `PhantomData`
to pretend like `HasThreadSubscriptionFn` is always part of the struct,
to avoid changing the auto trait implementations when the feature is
enabled.

signatures: Use VerifyingKey's TryFrom<&[u8]> implementation

… rather than converting the public key slice to an array manually and
then using `from_bytes`. If we create a `SignatureError` manually, there
are no details about the error, but if we use the upstream crate's
implementation we get an error message about the key's length.

This allows to serialize explicit values that Ruma previously assumed would be the default in the homeserver, which may not always be the case.

canonical_json: Add a serde::Serializer for CanonicalJsonValue

It allows to serialize a type directly to a `CanonicalJsonValue`, with
stricter rules than `serde_json::value::Serializer` to discourage from
relying on undocumented behavior.

This serializer is also used in `to_canonical_value()`.

xtask: Add command to update spec links

Using `latest` means that links in docs can break after a new spec
release which might also make CI fail.

The command can be run as `cargo xtask spec-links update`. It tries to
update all spec links that are not in `SpecLink::URL_ALLOWLIST` to the
`SpecLink::PREFERRED_VERSION`. The updated links are checked to exist,
and the user is warned to check those with duplicate fragments in the
spec to ensure that they still point to the proper part of the spec.

The code to check spec links was also refactored to reuse the code
between both tasks. Instead of allowing any spec version in the list
it now only allows URLs in the allowlist or using the preferred spec
version. This task can be run via 2 commands:
`cargo xtask ci spec-links` or `cargo xtask spec-links check`.

Update spec links

Update the links to point to the latest spec version (`v1.18`) rather
than to use `latest`. This will avoid links in docs to ever break after
a new spec release.

signatures: Ignore signatures from keys missing from the key map

I believe this was a misinterpretation of the spec:

> If it cannot find a verification key then the check fails.

This formulation is confusing, it could mean:

> If it cannot find **one of** the verification keys then the check
> fails.

which is what was implemented. It could also mean:

> If it cannot find **any** verification key then the check
> fails.

Which is what this change does. This also matches the behavior of
Synapse.

client-api: Handle non-compliant/corrupt fields in simplified sliding sync responses

Sometimes a malformed or corrupted value that's *supposed* to be a string
(e.g., a room name, avatar, or room hero display name or avatar MxcUri)
may be sent in a homeserver's SSS payload, which might be a homeserver problem
or a buggy client-side update.

This makes the *entire* sync payload invalid because ruma is strict about
deserializing it, which then causes the matrix-rust-sdk to fail to handle it
(e.g., the rooms list service fails and can't get updated, and then it flip-flops
between Online/Running and Offline, which is a pretty bad user experience).

Now we gracefully handle deserialization failures for those fields,
treating them as if they were absent from the sync v5 response entirely.

Added a new cargo feature `unstable-compat-lax-syncv5-deser` to enable this.

feat: Add a `zeroize` method on identifiers.

This patch adds the `zeroize(mut self)` method on identifiers, calling
the `zeroize` crate.

Note that identifiers **DO NOT** implement the `zeroize::Zeroize` trait
because the `zeroize::Zeroize::zeroize` method takes `&mut self`, which
means the identifiers would not be consumed, and then will contain
invalid data. That's why we implement a custom `zeroize(mut self)`
method consuming `self`.

api: Restructure OutgoingRequest

The following changes are made:

- Rename the main trait method from try_into_http_request to
  try_into_http_request_inner
- Make the main trait method non-generic, by introducing a new
  associated type Body, and changing the Ok return value from
  http::Request<T: Default + BufMut + AsRef<[u8]>> to
  http::Request<Self::Body>, where Body implements a new OutgoingBody
  trait that's responsible for serializing it
- Remove authentication from the main trait method, because it relies on
  being able to read the body bytes (for server-to-server signatures)
- Add trait OutgoingRequestExt that provides try_into_http_request with
  the same functionality / semantics as the previous
  OutgoingRequest::try_into_http_request.

This is useful for a number of reasons:

- Trait implementations can now be fully codegen'ed, which might be
  useful for downstream crates because their (own) compile times should
  be lowered since they no longer have to monomorphize these
  implementations (at the same time, the compile time of Ruma itself
  will likely increase, just like the on-disk size of the compiled API
  crates)
- We can likely reuse these trait impls as-is for CBOR serialization,
  should we ever implement that
- We can definitely reuse these trait impls for error-path-tracking
  serialization (though that is really much more interesting for
  *de*serialization)

If this gets approved, I will work on making the same sort of change to
the other API traits.

identifiers: Add SmallVec internal storage representation

Uses `smallvec::SmallVec<[u8; N]>` as internal representation, which
should allow to improve performance by allocating most identifiers on
the stack rather than on the heap.

The default size of the array on the stack is 32, but it can be
adjusted for each identifier type.

identifiers: Tweak length of inline arrays for SmallVec representation

These values come from tuwunel's implementation.

Some of them are justified by the Matrix specification:

- Event IDs are base64-encoded sha256 hashes, so their maximum length is
  known.
- Since room v12, room IDs are event IDs so they have the same length.
- `SpaceChildOrder` has a maximum length.

api: Add content_type method to OutgoingBody trait

It makes sense because the body should know its content type in most
cases, except in the few endpoints where the user can set it manually.

This allows to add the `Content-Type` HTTP header automatically in
`OutgoingRequestExt::try_into_http_request()` and
`OutgoingResponseExt::try_into_http_response()` rather than always have
to do it manually in `try_into_http_*_inner()`. If the request or
response type already sets the HTTP header in `try_into_http_*_inner()`
it is not overwritten.
